input.question: Why are indoor-only shopping malls dying in the USA?
input.ground_truth: Most indoor malls depend on the very large "anchor" stores to pull people in. These are your Macy's, Nordstrom, and other department stores, for the most part. These stores aren't doing nearly as well with the advent of online shopping, so the foot traffic to the other stores suffer. With less foot traffic, the smaller stores start to shutter, and it becomes a cycle. Strip malls are significantly less expensive and don't depend on their anchor stores in the same way.

Well, I remember hearing that more people are shopping online. So, maybe instead of going to the mall, they just buy things from their phones or computers. That makes sense because online shopping is convenient—you don't have to leave the house, and you can find a lot more options.

Another thing is that some stores are closing down. If a store isn't making enough money, they might have to close. So, if a mall has a lot of stores closing, the mall might not have enough businesses to stay open. That would make the mall less appealing to people who still go there.

Also, maybe people's preferences are changing. They might prefer going to places that have more things to do, like restaurants, entertainment, or maybe even outdoor spaces. So, if a mall is just indoor stores without anything else, people might not want to go there as much.

I should also consider the economy. If people are spending less money, they might not go shopping as often. That would affect the malls because they rely on people coming in to spend money.

So, putting it all together, the main reasons are online shopping, stores closing, changing preferences, and economic factors. But how do I explain this to a 5-year-old?
